text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE NATION
- Pakistan's Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said the fiscal budget 1997/98 (July-June) would not be a hard budget for the people as power, water and gas tariffs will not be raised.
- At least five people were killed and 40 wounded by a powerful bomb explosion in a house in Karachi.
- The three-member tribunal set up to investigate the death of Murtaza Bhutto, brother of ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto, has submitted its report to the government.
- More than 100 financial institutions, in 45 countries, are now practising some form of interest-free Islamic finance.
THE FRONTIER POST
- Pakistani-U.S. joint military exercises will begin in different parts of Punjab province in the second week of June.
- Work on the multi-billion dollar integrated Keti Bandar port project has been stopped because of non-fulfillment of a commitment by the Pakistani government.
- The Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd will have four million telephone connections by 1998.
THE NEWS
- Pakistan Air Force has started a court martial of an officer, Qasim Bhatti, for alleged involved in drug smuggling.
- Maulana Fazlur Rehman, leader of Jamiat-i-Ulema-i-Islam, has quit politics to pursue an Islamic revolution on the lines of Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said the government would abide by all agreements signed with private power companies.
DAWN
- The government has shelved the Karachi and Lahore mass rail transit projects in 1997/98 due to resource constraints.
- The Privatisation Commission, owed 1.4 billion rupees, is to be more stringent in getting payment of sale proceeds.
- U.S. textile tycoons have shown interest in buying a dozen sick textile units located in the central Punjab province.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Hafeezullah Ishaq, chairman of the Central Board of Revenue, said new income tax schemes would be introduced in the budget to reduce contact between tax payers and tax officers.

- The Punjab provincial government has decided to bring orchards covering more than 7.5 acres of land into the farm tax net, besides lowering tax exemption ceiling to 7.5 acres from 12.5 acres for irrigated cultivated land.
- Pakistan and China are studying a possible joint venture in marine pollution control at the ports.
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto will leave for Italy on Sunday for a six-day visit, a party spokesman said.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
